headline: 300 prisoners died while being taken to hospital in 5 years 9 months
summary: Out of 1,235 total deaths in prisons, nearly a quarter died during transit. Severe overcrowding and shortage of medical staff are cited as key reasons.
details: At least 300 prisoners died while being transported from prisons to hospitals between 2021 and September 28, 2024. This is part of a larger total of 1,235 prisoner deaths over the same period.
caption:
300 prisoners died while being transported to hospitals in less than 6 years. Overcrowding and medical shortages are the killing factors.

At least 300 prisoners died while being transported from prisons to hospitals between 2021 and September 28, 2024. This is part of a larger total of 1,235 prisoner deaths over the same period.

headline_marked: Trump and tech giants [[agree to self-regulate AI]] in White House accord
headline: Trump and tech giants agree to self-regulate AI in White House accord
summary: Top AI leaders from OpenAI, Nvidia, and Meta agree to a 'morally binding' commitment to build safeguards, while Trump renames the tech 'super intelligence'.
details: US President Donald Trump met with top AI leaders, including Jensen Huang of Nvidia, Greg Brockman of OpenAI, and Mark Zuckerberg of Meta, to discuss the regulation of artificial intelligence.
The executives signed the 'White House Accord,' a morally binding agreement to self-regulate and build adequate safeguards for the fast-moving technology, though it is not legally enforceable.

During the meeting, Trump officially renamed the technology 'super intelligence' (SI) via an executive order, stating that the term 'artificial intelligence' is inaccurate because the tech is not artificial.
Meta's Mark Zuckerberg noted that the accord aims to ensure AI works as intended, implementing robust internal controls and multiple layers of auditing, including external oversight.
Elon Musk described the agreement as executives 'grading each other's homework,' while other attendees included Jeff Bezos, Satya Nadella, and Sundar Pichai.
The meeting comes as US lawmakers face pressure to curb AI development due to fears of job displacement and societal upheaval, following safety breaches at OpenAI.
Trump has urged unfettered AI development to outpace China and fuel the US economy, dismissing warnings about existential risks to humanity as overblown.
The president also supported the expansion of data centers, suggesting that AI companies will be 'generous' to the communities that host these vast computing facilities.
caption:
Tech titans agree to 'police themselves' in a new White House accord. Trump officially renames AI to 'super intelligence'.

US President Donald Trump met with top AI leaders, including Jensen Huang of Nvidia, Greg Brockman of OpenAI, and Mark Zuckerberg of Meta, to discuss the regulation of artificial intelligence.

The executives signed the 'White House Accord,' a morally binding agreement to self-regulate and build adequate safeguards for the fast-moving technology, though it is not legally enforceable.

During the meeting, Trump officially renamed the technology 'super intelligence' (SI) via an executive order, stating that the term 'artificial intelligence' is inaccurate because the tech is not artificial.

Meta's Mark Zuckerberg noted that the accord aims to ensure AI works as intended, implementing robust internal controls and multiple layers of auditing, including external oversight.

Elon Musk described the agreement as executives 'grading each other's homework,' while other attendees included Jeff Bezos, Satya Nadella, and Sundar Pichai.

The meeting comes as US lawmakers face pressure to curb AI development due to fears of job displacement and societal upheaval, following safety breaches at OpenAI.

Trump has urged unfettered AI development to outpace China and fuel the US economy, dismissing warnings about existential risks to humanity as overblown.

The president also supported the expansion of data centers, suggesting that AI companies will be 'generous' to the communities that host these vast computing facilities.
